findings.reason: the plan must record §42 as done-except-its-regular-check clause handed to §51 (or fold §51 into §42), otherwise two implementable sections race the same file and §42's remainder is re-built twice.
findings.text: §51 is declared `implementable` beside §42, whose work landed on 8 November at `ce7a27b113` ("restart a declared service running code the checkout no longer carries"), not beside a done section; §42's own deliverable promised the restart "on its regular check", and its commit wired the comparison only into `reload()`, so §42's unsatisfied half and §51 are one requirement, in one file (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`), with no `plan-section-depends-on` entry linking them — a coordinator reading declarations can dispatch both into the same module

findings.reason: the plan's chain is the record a coordinator reads first; with no open followup naming §51 and §45's re-plan unrecorded, the new section is unreachable through the plan.
findings.text: every followup is now `resolved` (f-wns-001 … f-wns-005) while eight sections remain `implementable` (s4, s21, s23, s31, s35, s38, s42, s51) and none names §51, so the plan's own dispatch chain has no next step and a coordinator following it never dispatches the section this change adds

findings.reason: a node can close on the restart arm alone and leave the reporting clause unimplemented, and no negative control would show the guard fires.
findings.text: the deliverable requires that "a service whose stamp the supervisor cannot compare is reported, not silently adopted", but the done-when drives only the comparable case (old stamp, main moved, restart on the new stamp); the base code silently adopts when the current stamp is unreadable (`_runs_recorded_code`, fleet_supervisor.py:1438-1440, returns True with no log), so this clause ships unmeasured and unguarded

response_events.note: §42 is descoped with its unmet half, the restart on the regular check, carried by §51

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` exists, and every commit s51 cites resolves: `dc2eb54` (tree), `21ccbe709d`, `9e8e625126`, `b7e0f962b5`, `6fdeccc540`, `ce7a27b113`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s51's second deliverable clause ("a service whose stamp the supervisor cannot compare is reported, not silently adopted") has no arm and no negative control, so only half the deliverable is measured.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the run's note, the base-revision reproduction log and every gate log sit under the run directory, and the test and reproduction are on durable paths.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section names no symbol, file private to the fix or plan label, and its title carries only the plan's own §NN convention used by its neighbours.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated evidence supports the endpoint: `DeclaredServices._runs_recorded_code` (fleet_supervisor.py:1424) compares a copy's recorded stamp with the checkout's, and it is reached only from `reload()` (:1495, callers :2432, :2548, :2559), while the periodic `supervise_once` (:1702) restarts only exited copies, so a service can stay on an old stamp indefinitely and the named endpoint (restart within one check, reproducibly red at base) is reachable and checkable.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — both clauses govern one decision point in one module (what the declared-service stamp comparison decides); the unmeasured half is raised under done_when rather than as a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §51 is declared `implementable` while §42, which is declared `implementable` too, already has its 8 November commit on main and overlaps §51's endpoint in the same module; and no open followup names §51.
